title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
summary: The Federal Open Market Committee voted unanimously on January 27, 2021 to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and to continue asset purchases at the pace of at least $80 billion per month in Treasuries and at least $40 billion per month in agency mortgage-backed securities. The Committee formalized its new average inflation targeting framework, committing to maintain an accommodative stance until inflation has risen to 2 percent and is on track to moderately exceed 2 percent for some time, alongside achieving maximum employment.
key_points: Federal funds rate target range held at 0 to 1/4 percent, unanimous vote 11-0
Forward guidance tied to dual outcomes: maximum employment and 2% inflation with moderation above 2%
Asset purchase pace unchanged: at least $80bn/month Treasuries and at least $40bn/month MBS until substantial further progress
Adopted average inflation targeting framework—Committee will aim for inflation moderately above 2% for some time
Pace of economic recovery described as moderated in recent months with weakness concentrated in pandemic-affected sectors
Voting members: Jerome H. Powell (Chair), John C. Williams (Vice Chair), plus 9 additional members
why_it_matters: This statement represents the Fed's formal commitment to its post-2020 strategy review framework, signaling tolerance for above-target inflation as a trade-off for achieving maximum employment. The unchanged policy stance provided certainty to markets during a critical vaccination rollout period, while the explicit forward guidance on rate liftoff conditions anchored long-term rate expectations.
macro_context: The statement acknowledges the pandemic's continued economic toll, noting that inflation is running persistently below the 2% longer-run goal. This dovish framing—emphasizing labor market recovery as a co-equal objective—set the stage for extended accommodation. The average inflation targeting approach represented a significant policy evolution that justified prolonged low rates even if inflation temporarily overshot targets.
market_structure_context: Asset purchase language explicitly states these purchases help foster smooth market functioning and accommodative financial conditions, supporting the flow of credit to households and businesses. This confirms the Fed's QE program serves a market plumbing function beyond pure monetary stimulus.
